title: PBS Station Fears Losing 50TB of Data After Being Ghosted By Cloud Provider - Slashdot

content_html:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from Ars Technica: After its cloud storage provider went defunct, a PBS affiliate decided to sue a data center provider to regain access to 50TB of TV shows, videos, and other data dating back 70 years. As reported this week by Current, a trade newspaper covering public broadcasting, St. Louis affiliate Nine PBS filed a lawsuit against Iron Mountain Data Centers on July 28, seeking access to the data. In the litigation filed in Denver District Court, Nine PBS says that its cloud storage provider, Open Source Storage (OSS), used one of Iron Mountain's Denver data centers to store the channel's data. However, OSS is being unresponsive, and Nine PBS says Iron Mountain has refused to release its data.

The data in question includes the station's coverage of the COVID-19 pandemic, East St. Louis' history, The Great Flood of 1993, and over 11,000 files, The Denver Post reported in July. The lawsuit claims that "most" of the data is "unique and irreplaceable," according to the Post. Last month, a judge blocked Iron Mountain from deleting or modifying the data.

In a hearing on Wednesday, a judge ruled that Iron Mountain must hand over any physical devices holding the data, Current reported today. The judge also said that Nine PBS must find a third party, such as a former OSS worker, who can help retrieve the data within 30 days and without sharing or corrupting data belonging to other OSS clients. Nine PBS is already communicating with a former OSS employee "who is willing to help," the report said. If complications arise, such as from the data being encrypted, another hearing will be scheduled. Nine PBS and Iron Mountain must provide updates by September 14.

Iron Mountain's spokesperson said the company only provides physical infrastructure, such as the building, network connectivity, power, and environmental controls. "Our customers rent space for their servers and other hardware. These are the client's assets. We don't have access to the data on the hardware/servers because they belong to our customers," the company said.

If it granted "unauthorized access to third-party hardware without a court order," Iron Mountain said the company would violate basic data privacy protocols, breach its contract with OSS, and "potentially [expose] confidential data belonging to other clients of OSS."

content_html_zh:
一位匿名读者引用了 Ars Technica 的一篇报道：在其云存储提供商倒闭后，PBS 附属公司决定起诉一家数据中心提供商，以重新获得 70 年前 50TB 的电视节目、视频和其他数据的访问权限。 据覆盖公共广播的商业报纸 Current 本周报道，圣路易斯附属九号 PBS 于 7 月 28 日对铁山数据中心提起诉讼，寻求获取数据。 在向丹佛地方法院提起的诉讼中，九号 PBS 表示，其云存储提供商开源存储 (OSS) 使用 Iron Mountain 的丹佛数据中心之一来存储该频道的数据。 然而，OSS 没有做出回应，而 9 号 PBS 表示，Iron Mountain 拒绝公布其数据。 据《丹佛邮报》7 月报道，这些数据包括该电台对 COVID-19 大流行的报道、东圣路易斯的历史、1993 年的大洪水以及超过 11,000 个文件。 据《华盛顿邮报》报道，该诉讼声称“大多数”数据是“独特且不可替代的”。 上个月，一名法官阻止铁山公司删除或修改数据。 据《Current》今天报道，在周三的听证会上，法官裁定 Iron Mountain 必须交出所有保存数据的物理设备。 法官还表示，九号 PBS 必须找到第三方，例如前 OSS 工作人员，可以帮助在 30 天内检索数据，并且不会共享或损坏属于其他 OSS 客户端的数据。 报道称，第九频道 PBS 已经与一名前 OSS 员工进行了沟通，“他愿意提供帮助”。 如果出现复杂情况，例如数据被加密，将安排另一次听证会。 9 PBS 和 Iron Mountain 必须在 9 月 14 日之前提供更新。 铁山公司的发言人表示，该公司仅提供物理基础设施，例如建筑、网络连接、电力和环境控制。 “我们的客户为他们的服务器和其他硬件租用空间。 这些是客户的资产。 我们无法访问硬件/服务器上的数据，因为它们属于我们的客户，”该公司表示。

Iron Mountain 表示，如果“未经法院命令而允许对第三方硬件进行未经授权的访问”，该公司将违反基本数据隐私协议、违反与 OSS 的合同，并“可能会暴露属于 OSS 其他客户的机密数据”。
